22|   - "Picture scene": a small, elegant text button at the very top of each scene view, on the progress line row, right-aligned (not in a side panel, not floating). It requests the scene image for the route's scene id.
23|   - "Picture this": a small popover next to a mouse text selection, matching the original Lectoria's behaviour: it appears on mouseup (after a requestAnimationFrame) only when the trimmed selection is at least 3 characters and lies inside the scene text; it is centred horizontally above the selection with a small arrow (absolute inside the scene view: x = selection centre, y = selection top minus 8 px, translate(-50%, -100%)); any mousedown outside the popover dismisses it, and so do Escape, a sub-page or scene change, and starting a request. 24|   - Result placement: inline under the scene heading, inside the scene view, at most about 320 px tall (`object-fit: contain`), with its caption, a small "New"/"Saved" tag and a dismiss (×) button; loading and error states sit in the same slot. Why: the scene view becomes one clean centred column, the image sits next to the text it illustrates (as in the original), and the side panel had nothing else to hold. Remove the companion aside and the chat placeholder line; the image stays for the current scene across its sub-pages and clears on scene change.
25|   - Keep the image API, cookies, quota and budget logic unchanged apart from English copy; keep the image tests passing (update the strings they pin).
26|6. Fix from the task 8 screenshot: the scene heading must not show a focus ring on first load. Move focus to the heading only after an in-app scene navigation, not on the initial render.

28|8. Do not touch `public/music/manifest.json`, audio files, the CSP media-src, or the credits/converter scripts: another worker owns them. Read the manifest types only. If a credit string is generated by that worker's converter, leave it alone and note it.

Review a change like the senior developer who will be paged when it breaks.

  the functions it calls, the tests, the README.

  or behavior changes, grep every caller.

  that, and say which load you assumed.

   rounding, time zones), a caller broken by the change, a fix applied in one
   caller while the shared function stays broken.

   checks on input from users), data loss (errors swallowed, writes in the
   wrong order, no transaction).

   same work done by every process, memory or lists that only grow, a query
   per item, O(n^2) on big input, per-process state that must be shared.

   data writes, a bug fix) with no test that fails when it breaks. One good
   test, not coverage.

   loop) are suggestions; some software counts every millisecond.

   - reuse: the repo already has this helper (name the path)
